solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Military discharge, March 2?

parts.note: a march by protesters is a demo
B is the second letter, as in plan B or the B-side, so it can stand for 2

explanation.surface: A diary entry or order: someone's release from the forces is dated the second of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March 2' reads as a date, but March is a protest march and 2 is the second letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob is the informal British word for demobilisation, release from the armed forces.

clue.text: Well-meaning interference, not with dogwood and wild rye

indicators.note: not with tells us the abbreviation for with is to be left out of the shrub's name
wild means the letters of rye run untamed into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden scene: a busybody tidying a hedge of dogwood and some wild grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes W (with) from DOGWOOD, leaving DOGOOD; 'wild' turns RYE into ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the meddling of a do-gooder, someone whose kindly intentions turn into intrusive interference.

clue.text: Agreement that people may be delighted to strike?

definitions.text: Agreement that people may be delighted to strike?

parts.words: Agreement that people may be delighted to strike?
parts.note: a marriage is an agreement couples are happy to strike, and the thing struck to give light is a firelighting stick

explanation.surface: A deal both sides are thrilled to make.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'delighted' as 'de-lighted', given light: the strip you strike for a flame. A marriage, or a pairing, is also an agreement happily struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a marriage or pairing agreed upon and the small stick struck to make fire.

clue.text: OK, fund blown: mad, bad man's needed to resort to this?

indicators.note: money blown is squandered and scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wastrel has spent all the money and must now go cap in hand to someone for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown' shuffles OK FUND with MAD BAD MAN; the 's of man's is just 'is', joining to 'needed to'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a joking name for parents as the lender of last resort for grown-up children short of cash.

clue.text: Group of houses — about 12, on reflection?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: CA, for circa, means about
twelve is one dozen, written I DOZ with the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A query about a housing development: is it roughly a dozen homes, now one thinks about it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns CA + I DOZ (one dozen) backwards. The surface 'houses' are dwellings; in astrology the twelve signs are called houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrologers divide the heavens into twelve signs or houses, and the zodiac is that set taken together.

clue.text: Disguised Led Zeppelin's first fan in red or white?

indicators.note: first picks just the opening letter of the band's second word
something disguised has its appearance altered, so the band word changes its order

explanation.surface: A rock fan in disguise sneaks into a Led Zeppelin gig wearing red or white.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'fan in' as the fan coming in: Z, then IN, then FAN, then the disguised band word. Red and white here are wine colours, not a rock band's shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian grape makes a full red wine and also a pale pink 'white' version, so either colour fits.

clue.text: Some said it too

indicators.note: some of the words means the letters sit inside the following phrase

explanation.surface: Several people repeated the same remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' shows the letters run across saiD IT TOo, and the whole clue is also what the word means.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is a way of agreeing that the same thing applies again, as others put it before.

clue.text: Welcome spelunker who's out of credit

indicators.note: a person out of something lacks it, so the letters standing for credit are removed

parts.note: a spelunker explores caves, a caver
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A cave explorer who has run out of money is greeted anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's out of' takes CR out of CAVER, leaving AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin salutation used as a greeting, the hail with which Romans and Caesar's legions bade someone welcome.

clue.text: Prepare for storm, Britain: where's man cutting straw roofs, 5?

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for Britain or British
the second half of this answer sits in the grid at entry 10 down, so where it is gives at ten down

indicators.note: one piece cutting another goes into it, so the word for a man is put inside

parts.note: roofs made of straw are thatches
HE is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A storm warning for Britain, with a thatcher hard at work on straw roofs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where's' asks where the rest of the phrase sits: AT TEN DOWN, its place in the grid. The closing '5?' is DITTO, saying that rest is likewise the man in the roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors fasten wooden battens over hatch covers before bad weather, and the idiom means getting ready for trouble.

clue.text: Order anything en suite — it's time for slap and tickle!

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A couple at a hotel ring room service from their en suite room before some saucy fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like room service, but it rearranges ANYTHING EN SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1890s are remembered as a permissive, frivolous era, a period of playful flirtation; slap and tickle is British slang for it.

clue.text: Reciprocated wisdom?

parts.note: wisdom suggests a wisdom tooth, and reciprocation is giving one in return, an eye-for-an-eye exchange

explanation.walkthrough: 'wisdom' is a wisdom tooth; paying one back with another is the Old Testament rule of retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase describes exact retaliation, an injury repaid with the same injury.

clue.text: See 7
Having alphabetical reference but no X? Yes!

indicators.note: but no letter means that one letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a book with an alphabetical list of references is indexed

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry about a book index that skips the letter X, followed by an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no' removes X from INDEXED.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic word of agreement, used to say certainly or truly.

clue.text: Clergyman immersed in flatpacking guide?

indicators.note: something immersed in another is surrounded by it, so the clergyman goes inside

parts.note: assembling flatpack furniture is do-it-yourself, DIY
a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar is absorbed in following the instructions for assembling flatpack furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatpacking' stands for do-it-yourself because flatpack furniture is assembled at home by the buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A book listing names, addresses or numbers serves as a reference handbook to find people.

clue.text: Laid-back children redo Mucha frames, more art deco than nouveau

indicators.note: laid back reads as lying backwards, so the letters are reversed
the phrase frames the letters, holding them within its words

explanation.surface: Relaxed kids redo the frames on Mucha prints in a later style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' holds the letters in childRENREDOMucha and 'Laid-back' reverses them. Alphonse Mucha was an Art Nouveau poster artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco followed Art Nouveau, so it is the more recent and up-to-date of the two styles.

clue.text: To Frenchman, what's for slicing red German cheese?

indicators.note: a blade slicing something passes into it, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: rot is German for red
que is French for what

explanation.surface: A puzzled question to a Frenchman about what to use when cutting a red German cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenchman' and 'German' are language signals: the word for 'what' comes from French and the colour from German.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-veined ewe's-milk variety from southern France, ripened in caves at Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

clue.text: Label of Old Glory torn in plan to retreat

indicators.note: in here places the scrambled letters within the reversed plan
to retreat is to go backwards, so the plan is read in reverse

parts.note: a map is a plan

indicators.note: torn apart, the letters of the word are scattered

explanation.surface: A torn American flag features in a plan for military withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Glory looks like one unit (the US flag), but 'Old' ends the definition. 'torn' turns GLORY to OLYGR; 'to retreat' reverses MAP to PAM, which holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A former record company, defunct since its absorption into Universal, so a label from the past.

clue.text: Question One in set: How is the Japanese medlar also known?

definitions.text: How is the Japanese medlar also known?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the set

parts.note: a lot is a set of items, as at an auction
A means one, as in a pound

explanation.surface: A quiz: question one in the set asks for another name for a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange Asian fruit tree goes by an alternative common name, the Japanese medlar.

clue.text: Totally against experimental research, morally speaking

parts.note: in all means in total
con means against, as in pros and cons
experimental research is science

explanation.surface: An ethical objection to animal testing or other lab work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means honestly or by any fair moral standard, appealing to conscience.

clue.text: Characteristic of student's first digs

parts.note: like means typical of, as in that is just like him

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the student

explanation.surface: A student's first lodgings are typical of student life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like lodgings, but it is the slang verb: he digs jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, someone who digs something enjoys or appreciates it.

clue.text: Very distressed tradespeople, it would seem

indicators.note: it would seem flags that the answer only appears to describe the workers when read as an instruction

parts.note: the TUC, the British Trades Union Congress, stands for tradespeople; written upward in a down entry it gives the first word

explanation.surface: Workers in the trades look deeply upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the UK's Trades Union Congress. In a down light, 'up' means read upward, so the answer read as wordplay says 'the TUC, going up'.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for being badly upset or hurt in feelings.

clue.text: Enquire if press boss is taken by cloudy beer like this?

indicators.note: taken by the next piece means the earlier pieces come after it

parts.note: C stands for cloudy in weather-map shorthand
to enquire is to ask
if introduces a condition
an editor runs a newspaper, ED for short

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether a newspaper editor has been won over by a hazy pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken by' shows ASK, CONDITION and ED coming after C. C for cloudy is weather-map shorthand; 'cloudy beer' looks like one phrase, but 'cloudy' gives C and 'beer like this?' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale finishes maturing in the cask, often looking hazy, so such beer is matured that way.

clue.text: Test 19? 5 — it will

indicators.note: the answer to 19 down, read as cut up, says the test word is docked and then turned upward in this down light

parts.note: a test is an exam; the 19 instruction leaves its opening three letters to work on

explanation.surface: A cryptic chain of cross-references about testing a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is CUT UP: cut removes M from EXAM and up reverses EXA in a down light. 5 is DITTO, so the definition says it will cut up as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopping tool is the very thing that will hack wood into pieces.

clue.text: I agree about judge going over the top

indicators.note: going over means turning back over, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: yes says I agree
re means about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a judge has behaved outrageously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the top' reads as excessive, but 'going over' reverses YES + RE + J and 'top' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover is a garment worn on the upper body, a top.

clue.text: Bus station's record during period

indicators.note: during puts the record within the period

parts.note: a dot is a period, a full stop
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A bus station's punctuality record over some period.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage where buses are kept and serviced is the usual meaning of this word in transport.
